after: An edited policy is inoperative until a human re-attests it. Attestation establishes which bytes are operative, and it says nothing about which bytes a given decision was made under, so a policy edit that lands between a request and its grant leaves the log unable to show whether the approver decided by the rules the requester was routed by. The runtime therefore records the attested SHA-256 on `approval.requested` and on `approval.granted`, assigned by the runtime at the write boundary exactly as `ts` is (§8), with a caller-supplied value refused on the same structural grounds. A grant whose attested hash differs from the hash pinned on the matching request MUST be refused with its own machine-readable reason, distinct from the unattested-policy refusal: the autonomy, limits, and TTL that put the question in front of a human are no longer in force, so the pending request is void, and the action is requested again under the policy that now governs it. Records written before this field existed carry no hash and are decided as they always were, following the additive-change rule of §8. (Amended APRV-118, pending sign-off.)
